DI428* is a group of ICD-10 diagnosis codes used within the Danish healthcare system to identify cases of heart failure. It serves as a critical component in the technical definition of the [[hjertesvigtsindikatoren|Hjertesvigtsindikatoren]] (Heart Failure Indicator), which is designated as Indicator 15 in the AFDK (Atrial Fibrillation Database) quality assurance framework [^src1]. 

Within the context of the 2025 AFDK report, Indicator 15 measures the incidence of heart failure within one year following a new diagnosis of atrial fibrillation [^src1]. To calculate this metric, data is drawn from the Danish National Patient Register (Landspatientregisteret), where a heart failure event is strictly defined as a hospital contact with heart failure recorded as either a primary (A) or secondary (B) diagnosis [^src1]. DI428* is one of several specific ICD-10 code groups—including DI50*, DI110*, DI130*, DI132*, DI420*, DI426*, DI427*, and DI429*—that qualify a hospital contact as a heart failure event for this indicator [^src1]. 

The use of these specific diagnostic codes allows researchers and health authorities to track the quality of care and the clinical outcomes of atrial fibrillation patients on a national scale. However, the 2025 report also notes limitations related to the underlying registry data, such as the lack of coverage for general practice, underreporting of unrecognized atrial fibrillation, and potential registration issues driven by DRG-based incentives [^src1].
